newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: World Bank cautions Philippines on forex loans.
newsitem.headline: World Bank cautions Philippines on forex loans.

text.p: The World Bank on Thursday cautioned Manila against the increasing number of foreign exchange loans given out by Philippine banks to the private sector.

The bank, in a report on the country, said most banks' foreign exchange inflows came from foreign currency deposit units (FCDU) which are short term while the loans they granted were mainly long term.
The bank urged the government to take measures to limit the maturity mismatches.
The 22 page report was prepared for a meeting of donor countries which met in Tokyo on Wednesday and approved aid pledges worth $2.9 billion to the Philippines.

The bank, while praising the country's gross national product growth of 7.1 percent in the first nine months of 1996 compared to 5.3 percent in the same period last year, said the Philippines needed to raise its tax collections and savings rate

The Philippines this year is expected to post a budget surplus for the second straight year but economists have said that this was mainly a result of one time gains coming from privatisating state-owned assets. With income from this source diminishing, the country needs to have a sustainable source of revenue.
The present tax system has many loopholes which allows largescale tax evasion but it is due to be changed with the government recently approving a new tax law.
